title: KVCache session entropy notes
content:
Objective:
Quick running notes / reproduce checklist for weird per-session token jitter we saw overnight: duplicated tokens + sudden kernel fallback that correlates with very long prefix sessions (> 32k tokens) when continuous batching is active. Trying to capture commands, traces, hypotheses, and minimal repros before filing a proper bug report.

Observed symptom summary:
- Some user sessions (rare, maybe 1/10k requests) return duplicated token fragments or truncated continuations after a long prefix (20k+ tokens).
- Investigation shows serving runtime switches attention kernel mid-request (flash_attn -> fallback_attn) and KV cache offsets for that session appear shifted by a non-constant delta (not a simple +1).
- Happens more when we have high batching (batcher size > 16) + mixed sequence lengths in the batch.
- Suspected relation to KV index wraparound / slot reuse when the session's cached KV is large and the GC/eviction runs concurrently.

Quick commands I ran (local dev box, linux):
- Capture runtime logs for a reproducer: 
  sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -f | grep --line-buffered "session_id=\"sess" > /tmp/runtime-tail.log &
  ./tools/infer_client --model redwood-v0-3b --session-id sess-entropy-01 --prefix-file long-prefix.txt --streaming false --profile > /tmp/infer-out.txt 2>&1

- Profiling with env vars: 
  RUNTIME_DEBUG=kv:trace,KERNEL:info ./run_server --config=local-dev.yaml > server-verbose.log 2>&1

Snippets from logs (redacted):
- runtime-tail.log: 
  [2025-01-20 03:22:17.893] INFO  session_id=\"sess-entropy-01\" kv_cache:lookup slot=0x4f3a shard=3 found=TRUE offset=0x1a3
  [2025-01-20 03:22:17.920] WARN  session_id=\"sess-entropy-01\" attention:kernel_switch from=flash_attn to=fallback_attn reason=seqlen_transition predicted=8192 actual=8196
  [2025-01-20 03:22:17.922] ERROR session_id=\"sess-entropy-01\" kv_cache:read mismatch expected_offset=0x1a3 actual_offset=0x1ff delta=0x5c
  [2025-01-20 03:22:17.925] ERROR session_id=\"sess-entropy-01\" output:token_stream duplicate_fragment=\"...the quick brown\"

- stack trace from server-verbose.log (short):
  at kv_cache::read_impl (kv_cache.cc:478)
  at kv_cache::get_kv_slice (kv_cache.cc:521)
  at attention::prepare_kv (attention.cc:1021)
  at session::run_forward (session.cc:341)
  at api::handle_request (api_handler.cc:214)

Repro attempts and results:
- deterministic minimal: used synthetic long-prefix (repeats of 1024-token block) to reach 24k tokens; continuous batching OFF -> cannot reproduce.
- batching ON (concurrency=8, batch_size=24) + mixed seqlen (some requests short ~128 tokens) -> reproduce reliably in ~10 runs.
- switching quantization (int8 vs int4) had no immediate effect.
- forcing kernel choice to flash_attn for whole request (override in config) suppresses duplication but increases latency and occasionally triggers OOM on large batches.
- toggling KV ttl (from default 24h to short 5m) did not change repro frequency (so not pure TTL eviction).

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
1) KV slot aliasing due to wraparound: when KV index increments and backend GC runs concurrently, an in-flight read may map to a recently freed slot that has been re-used for another session’s KV. This would explain non-constant delta.
   - counterpoint: cache lookup logs include shard and slot id; in the error case shard matched but offset didn't. Means mapping exists but offsets diverge.
2) Kernel selection path sets up different KV addressing scheme (pack vs aligned) and code paths use different offset base (e.g., flash_attn expects 16-byte-aligned KV blocks, fallback uses 8-byte and we are applying wrong stride when switching mid-request).
   - supporting evidence: kernel_switch log precedes offset mismatch by ~2-3ms.
3) Continuous-batching merge code incorrectly adjusts per-session kv_offset when concatenating requests of different prefix lengths, producing stale offset for tail of merged batch. This would explain the correlation with high batch sizes and mixed seqlen.
4) Race where eviction/compaction re-writes KV index table while session thread reads an entry; read uses a not-yet-atomic two-step that can see index update half-applied.

Local tests to discriminate hypotheses (todo checklist):
- [ ] Add extra logging: atomic generation id for KV index entries and include gen_id in lookup and read. If mismatch, we can detect concurrent rewrite.
- [ ] Force kernel switch to be pre-declared at request start (no mid-request switching) and run batch reproducer. If stops happening -> hypothesis #2 gains weight.
- [ ] Run with batcher disabled but with manual request coalescing to see if the concatenate code is at fault (#3).
- [ ] Add mem-fence around KV table updates (temporary instrument) to see if frequency drops (#4).

Immediate mitigation ideas (short term):
- Disable kernel switching mid-request (config flag): not ideal but reduces incidence.
- Reduce max batch size for customers hitting large prefixes.
- Introduce aggressive per-session KV pinning when prefix length > threshold (so GC won't reclaim slots used by long-lived sessions).

Note about kernel thresholds:
- flash_attn -> fallback transition is currently triggered by dynamic seqlen heuristics; the transition point observed in logs is between 8192 and 8196 tokens (we had a tuned boundary). Need to audit boundary rounding logic (off-by-one case?) that could cause an unexpected kernel flip for batched requests which combine different seqlens.

Small repro script (local) used to hit the case:
  #!/bin/bash
  PREFIX=long-prefix-24k.txt # generated by repeating block_x1024.txt 24 times
  for i in {1..40}; do
    ./tools/infer_client --model redwood-v0-3b --session-id sess-test-$i --prefix-file $PREFIX --batch-coalesce true --coalesce-size 24 --sleep-random 0.01 &
  done
  wait

Additional artifacts saved: /tmp/repro-dumps/ (saved kv-index dump + per-session metadata at time of failure).

Important traces to attach when filing bug:
- full server-verbose.log around failure window
- per-session KV index dump (kv_index.*.bin) and mapping table snapshot
- infer_client stdout/stderr for reproducer
- heap/oom traces if any

Open questions / things to check before escalate:
- Is the KV index allocator using stable generation counters? (I think we had a TODO to add gen counters in early 2024).
- Does the attention kernel prepare_kv path mutate any per-session metadata that the batcher expects to be immutable mid-batch?
- Are we compressing offsets when serializing between CPU and GPU with different endianness/alignment on certain cloud types (we saw an old bug on g4dn where stride assumptions were wrong)?

Next actions (my plan):
- Today: add gen_id logging to kv_cache::lookup and kv_cache::read (quick patch) and run the 40x reproducer in dev; collect traces. (PR draft: GH #4217)
- If gen_id mismatches observed -> file high-priority bug and schedule immediate mitigation (disable mid-request kernel switching).
- If no gen mismatch -> force no mid-request kernel switch and rerun; if repro stops -> focus on kernel code paths.
- Loop in Ethan and Lina: Ethan for batcher and concatenation code, Lina for kernel selection path and attention.cc review.

Notes / thoughts to myself:
- This has the smell of a classic race between allocator and reader; those are nasty because reproducer can be timing-sensitive. Increase randomness in sleep in reproducer; run on a two-socket machine to vary thread scheduling.
- Keep reproduction artifacts lean; put a clear README in /tmp/repro-dumps with exact commands + server git hash.

If anyone picks this up: start by running the reproducer with RUNTIME_DEBUG=kv:trace,K_KERNEL:debug and attach server-verbose.log. Do not wipe /tmp/repro-dumps until we have a full KV index binary snapshot.

End of scratchpad.
